# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 49 (Bi-Vb Pc49)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc49  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 49  
**Title (English, from literature):** Studying worldly subjects  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tiracchānavijjāpariyāpuṇana-sikkhāpada* ("Training rule on studying worldly subjects"), cataloged as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 49, is a disciplinary rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka prohibiting Buddhist nuns from studying worldly arts or pointless knowledge (*tiracchānavijjā*) [Hüsken 1997]. An infraction of this rule constitutes a *pācittiya* offense requiring confession. Modern translation into English has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

As noted by Ute Hüsken, this rule forms a closely matched pair with the subsequent rule, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 50: while Pācittiya 49 prohibits learning or studying (*pariyāpuṇeyya*), Pācittiya 50 prohibits teaching (*vāceyya*) such worldly knowledge [Hüsken 1997]. Except for the operative verb, the rule phrasing, word commentary, casuistry, and non-offense (*anāpatti*) formulas of the two texts are virtually identical [Hüsken 1997].

 It corresponds to the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 49) and *Parivāra* (Pc 49), as well as corresponding rules in the Dharmaguptaka (e.g., Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 117), Mahīśāsaka (Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc 144, Pc 190), Sarvāstivāda (Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc 140), and Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinayas in Chinese (Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 150) and Tibetan (xct-mu-bi-vb-pc106).
